<italic>DUX4</italic>-driven gene expression, whereas muscle biopsies taken before treatment revealed high levels of <italic>DUX4</italic> expression [<citation rid="B164-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1212/WNL.0000000000200757" pmid="35750498" count="1">164</citation>]. <sentence_start/>These outcomes confirm previous molecular studies on the sensitivity of DUX4 to p38 inhibitors.

As an increasing amount of evidence has indicated that oxidative stress can contribute to the disease pathophysiology, the use of antioxidants is another intriguing treatment that can control or delay oxidative insults and potentially aid in maintaining FSHD muscle function. <sentence_start/>In vitro studies have already demonstrated the obvious advantages of antioxidant compounds on the morphology and phenotype of dystrophic muscle, increasing its resistance to pro-oxidant-mediated damage [<citation rid="B165-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1186/2044-5040-4-4" pmid="24484587" pmcid="PMC3914678" count="1">165</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Furthermore, the use of the antioxidant tempol improved myotube formation by decreasing DUX4-induced cytotoxicity [<citation rid="B109-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2016.08.007" pmid="27519269" count="1">109</citation>].

Along with the use of selenium and zinc, the effects of vitamins C and E on dystrophic patients have also been examined. <sentence_start/>Recent work has shown that these co-treatments enhanced muscle function in patients with FSHD [<citation rid="B166-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2014.09.014" pmid="25246239" count="1">166</citation>]. <sentence_start/>However, there is still a lack of clinical evidence about antioxidants being used to treat patients with FSHD. <sentence_start/>Further research will be needed.

Clinical observations are critical for moving clinical trials forward and securing treatment approval. <sentence_start/>Analyses of FSHD are very important, since they are also designed to assess muscle and physical function in FSHD patients. <sentence_start/>This is significant because, whereas the tests used for people with other neuromuscular disorders and dystrophies are typically very comparable, they are not always totally appropriate for patients with FSHD [<citation rid="B167-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1097/MRR.0000000000000444" pmid="33165002" pmcid="PMC7884240" count="1">167</citation>]. <sentence_start/>However, specific measurement methods for FSHD have been developed in recent years and many more are in the pipeline. <sentence_start/>These include functional outcome measures, particularly the FSHD Composite Outcome Measure (FSHD-COM) and Reachable Workspace (RWS) [<citation rid="B168-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1002/mus.26088" pmid="29381807" pmcid="PMC6066464" count="1">168</citation>,<citation rid="B169-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.nmd.2019.05.006" pmid="31345604" pmcid="PMC6996236" count="1">169</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Furthermore, two specific parameters, the FSHD Health Index (FSHD-HI) and FSHD-Rasch Constructed Overall Disability Scale (FSHD-RODS), are still used to evaluate the clinical treatment of FSHD [<citation rid="B59-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1002/mus.20522" pmid="16508966" count="1">59</citation>]. <sentence_start/>These aspects, however, will not be discussed in this review but are mentioned to emphasize the significance of the development and study of new therapeutic options, both clinical and molecular, for this complex disease. <sentence_start/>In addition, the alternative strategies described above and those that have been used to date are based on these clinical outcomes.
7.3. <sentence_start/>Possible Cancer Therapeutic Treatments Applicable for FSHD

As already mentioned in the preceding paragraphs, DUX4 has recently been discovered to have an altered expression also in a variety of cancers. <sentence_start/>In addition, several investigations are being conducted in this field of study to determine how to act on the possible modulation of DUX4 in tumor cells. <sentence_start/>In this final brief paragraph, we will examine some recent intriguing results that could be investigated and applied in future studies on the modulation of DUX4 in muscle cells affected by FSHD.

Ponatinib, an inhibitor of several tyrosine kinases, is the first chemical utilized in oncological therapy. <sentence_start/>There are ongoing studies to determine whether this inhibitor plays a role in the control of <italic>DUX4</italic> expression as well as muscle alterations in FSHD patients. <sentence_start/>Indeed, this inhibitor acts on several kinases involved in the regulation of DUX4 also in muscle cells [<citation rid="B170-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.molmed.2021.03.008" pmid="33863674" count="1">170</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Proteostasis inhibitors, such as carfilzomib and bortezomib, are also commonly utilized in cancer research and are of interest for DUX4 regulation [<citation rid="B171-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1021/acs.jmedchem.8b01943" pmid="30964987" pmcid="PMC7675178" count="1">171</citation>,<citation rid="B172-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.drudis.2010.01.008" pmid="20116451" count="1">172</citation>,<citation rid="B173-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1371/journal.pone.0186924" pmid="29107984" pmcid="PMC5673231" count="1">173</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Alterations to the protein degradation pathway, particularly changes to the proteasome’s correct functioning, have long been suspected of being involved in the start of the dystrophic phenotype, as these processes create protein clumps that injure muscle cells [<citation rid="B174-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1002/acn3.158" pmid="25750920" pmcid="PMC4338956" count="1">174</citation>,<citation rid="B175-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.3390/ijms21176429" pmid="32899400" pmcid="PMC7503226" count="1">175</citation>]. <sentence_start/>These are some of the chemical compounds used in oncology that have also been shown to inhibit DUX4 in cancer cells [<citation rid="B170-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.molmed.2021.03.008" pmid="33863674" count="1">170</citation>,<citation rid="B176-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/s41598-019-55752-0" pmid="31941891" pmcid="PMC6962364" count="1">176</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Because they act on cellular pathways that are disrupted in this kind of dystrophy and in DUX4, they may play an important role in future scientific studies to develop additional therapeutic options for this neuromuscular disorder.
8. <sentence_start/>Conclusions and Future Perspectives

In this review, we discuss differentiation and regeneration in muscle tissue, analyzing some altered cellular and molecular aspects typical of FSHD, the third most common form of muscular dystrophy. <sentence_start/>It is well known that FSHD is caused by a number of distinct genetic and epigenetic abnormalities, all of which result in the aberrant production of the <italic>DUX4</italic> transcription factor. <sentence_start/>When expressed, DUX4 triggers a series of events that culminate in cell death, which hinders muscle growth and repair [<citation rid="B135-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.3390/ijms21030729" pmid="31979100" pmcid="PMC7037115" count="1">135</citation>]. <sentence_start/>It has recently been discovered that DUX4 can interact with MRF proteins, altering their expression and causing incorrect myogenesis. <sentence_start/>Cellular and molecular studies are important to better understand the still unknown function of DUX4. <sentence_start/>All of this is critical for identifying new regulators of <italic>DUX4</italic> expression and attempting to block its aberrant expression, which results in the blockage of the pathways in which it appears to be involved. <sentence_start/>Furthermore, recent studies, which we have discussed above, may aid in the development of inhibitory therapeutic strategies. <sentence_start/>We attempt to summarize the most recent major discoveries of new inhibitors that could represent promising future therapeutic opportunities in this field. <sentence_start/>We have also discussed some gene therapies that are being researched in this field and that are still being continuously improved and updated today. <sentence_start/>Finally, we have summarized the few pharmaceutical strategies that have received the most attention in FSHD to date. <sentence_start/>In this regard, a number of researchers are developing treatment strategies that target DUX4 by either preventing the production of <italic>DUX4</italic> mRNA [<citation rid="B103-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1074/jbc.RA118.002633" pmid="29899111" pmcid="PMC6066320" count="1">103</citation>,<citation rid="B177-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ymthe.2018.04.019" pmid="29759937" pmcid="PMC6035737" count="1">177</citation>] or by employing AONs to specifically target <italic>DUX4</italic> mRNA [<citation rid="B147-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1093/hmg/ddw015" pmid="26787513" count="1">147</citation>,<citation rid="B178-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/mt.2016.111" pmid="27378237" pmcid="PMC5023379" count="1">178</citation>,<citation rid="B179-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/mt.2012.68" pmid="22508491" pmcid="PMC3392971" count="1">179</citation>]. <sentence_start/>The first DUX4-targeted treatments are either already under investigation or are proceeding to in vivo testing and eventual clinical approval. <sentence_start/>Of them, one phase-2 clinical trial of losmapimod ( ) which attempts to suppress or reduce <italic>DUX4</italic> expression in skeletal muscle is already ongoing, leading us to better understand the function of DUX4 in the pathogenesis of FSHD [<citation rid="B180-ijms-24-09503" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1186/s13395-022-00287-8" pmid="35039091" pmcid="PMC8762812" count="1">180</citation>].

In conclusion, more research is needed to fully understand the DUX4-mediated scenery complex that underpins FSHD and to develop effective treatments capable of correcting the cellular and molecular defects that cause serious damage to muscle homeostasis.
